title: Console Tooling Standup - 2026-06-30
content:
Attendees: Priya, Liam, Sofia, Daniel, Asha (join: 10m)

Status pulse (high level):
- UI: New rollout config page (phase 1) is UI-complete; waiting on backend feature flags API. Visual review scheduled Thurs.
- Rollouts: Canary engine integration tests passing locally; staging run flagged higher-than-expected error-rate on 95th pct latency when canary is scaled to 10%.
- Analytics: Latency dashboard (per-route + per-model) prototype pushed to staging; token-cost breakdown query optimizations in progress.

Detailed updates:
1) UI (Liam, Sofia)
- What went well: New rollout-config form complete, validation wired for % traffic allocation and time windows. Component tests added.
- Next: Hook to backend /api/rollouts/v1/create (pending API contract changes). Mock flows shown in demo.
- Blockers: Backend currently returns 422 for nested policy objects (see JIRA-3421). Need API change or frontend to flatten payload.

2) Rollouts & Runtime (Priya, Daniel)
- What went well: Canary routing shim implemented and deployed on staging; traffic splitting logic honours user-level overrides.
- Next: Increase canary scale in staging with synthetic load to replicate 95th pct latency spike.
- Blockers: Intermittent KV-cache misses under burst leading to regeneration overhead. Investigating correlation with batcher flush timing. Tracked in JIRA-3490.

3) Analytics & Observability (Asha)
- What went well: New per-route latency dashboard merged to feature branch; sampling for trace links working (1%).
- Next: Add token-cost heatmap and per-deployment cost attribution; validate with billing slice for last 7 days.
- Blockers: Prometheus query is expensive for the token-cost calculation; trying pre-aggregation in ClickHouse.

Decisions / Discussion points:
- We agreed to pause scaling canary >10% in production until KV-cache miss root cause is identified. (Action: Priya to own triage)
- For immediate unblock on UI, two options: change API to accept flattened policy OR implement adapter in frontend. Team prefers API change for long-term consistency but will ship frontend adapter as fallback if API change ETA > 2 days. (Owner: Liam + Daniel to coordinate with infra)

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Priya: Run extended staging canary with synthetic load, capture flamegraphs and batcher timings. Due: 2026-07-02.
- Daniel: Open PR to add adapter on frontend to flatten policy for rollout create payload (if API change delayed). Due: 2026-07-01.
- Liam: Coordinate API contract update request with backend team; add acceptance tests to prevent regressions. Due: 2026-07-01.
- Asha: Prototype ClickHouse pre-aggregation query for token-cost metric and share perf numbers. Due: 2026-07-06.

Risks / Notes:
- If KV-cache misses persist, canary exposure could cause higher inference costs and poor tail latency for customer traffic. Keep canary traffic capped.
- Need to communicate temporary pause to PM/CS for any customers expecting immediate rollout feature (SRE/CS pinged).

Quick wins for next week:
- Ship frontend adapter if API change delayed >48h to unstick demo for sales.
- Add a lightweight Prometheus recording rule for token-count per-route to reduce query cost.

Meeting artifacts & links:
- Demo recording (staging flows): https://zoom.us/rec/share/example-demo
- CI run for canary tests: https://ci.redwood-infra/builds/console-canary-2026-06-30

Notes to self:
- Remember to update rollout docs in Confluence after API change.
- Check with billing about a one-off cost report for canary runs this month.

Next standup: 2026-07-07 (same time).
